meta.status: PROVISIONAL automatic labels; no human (pharmacist) label used

closed_grounded.answer: Yes, roughly: within closed-book answers the seven paper checkers pass 4.9-18.1% of automatic unit/basis errors under the pre-registered labels (n = 447; all answers 6.5-19.0%) and 4.2-18.4% under the v2 labels (n = 425) — only Llama-3.3-70B RAGAS-NLI and MedScore (Mistral-Small-24B) fall below 7% — because 447 of 459 (v1) / 425 of 426 (v2) automatic errors are closed-book anyway; what changes in closed-book is PASS on correct answers, which drops to 41.8-74.8% (all answers 65.4-87.5%).

subtypes.reconciliation: Reconciliation: rule A reproduces the audit's 259/131 exactly under v1; rule B gives 255/129 and rule C 253/124, so the ad hoc 255/123 is not reproduced exactly by any committed rule (its first number equals rule B, its second is closest to rule C; the ad hoc rule was never committed, so it cannot be checked further). Under v2, rule A gives 259/98: the 33 fewer 'relative for absolute' items are exactly the m² superscript artefacts (answer per m², label per-m² unit unreadable). The paper should use rule A because it is the comparison that produced the error class itself, and should report the v2 figure alongside (and the adjudicated figure once available).

sensitivity.note: The 72 no-dose answers were never scored by any checker (scored set = 5,688 = 5,760 - 72), and the 4 parseable ones fall in unverifiable (3) / time_ambiguous (1), which are in neither the error nor the correct set; the main-table PASS rates with the parseable no-dose answers included under their v2 class are therefore identical to the v2 rates (rd2_rates_all.csv, label_set v2). A sensitivity with human labels is defined in prereg/rd2_amendment_1.md section 2.
